image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a common iguana resting on a textured surface (likely rock or wood). The image focuses on the head, neck, and forelimb. The iguana displays characteristic green and greyish coloration with a prominent dorsal crest of spines along the neck. The skin texture shows detailed granular scales on the body and larger plate-like scales on the head. One forelimb is clearly visible with distinct digits and claws.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is large and triangular with a prominent dewlap (loose skin fold) hanging from the throat.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head shape is consistent with an iguana, appearing robust and somewhat triangular. A dark, loose fold of skin (dewlap) is visible under the jawline, though partially shadowed.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are large with round pupils and golden irises.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eye is located on the far right edge of the frame and is heavily cropped/occluded by the angle and lighting. While a sliver of the eye socket is visible, the pupil shape and iris color cannot be definitively verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: A large circular subtympanic shield (scale) is present below the tympanum.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A large, distinct, circular scale pattern is visible on the cheek area, consistent with the location and appearance of the subtympanic shield.
The visible portion of the torso appears thick and muscular, fitting the description of a robust body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Coloration is bright green in juveniles, becoming darker green to greyish-green in adults with broad black bands on the body and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The iguana exhibits a mix of olive green, yellowish-green, and grey tones. There are darker shading/banding patterns visible on the neck and shoulder area, consistent with adult coloration.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Row of enlarged, spine-like scales running from the nape along the midline of the back to the tail base, forming a serrated crest.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A very prominent, sharp, serrated crest of spines runs along the neck and upper back, clearly matching the diagnostic feature.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is covered in small, granular scales with larger, plate-like scales on the head.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The texture differentiation is clear: the head features larger, smoother-looking plates, while the neck and body show fine, bead-like granular scales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are long and muscular with five clawed digits on each foot.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The front left limb is fully visible. It is muscular, and five distinct digits with claws are clearly resolved. No fusion or extra digits are observed.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and longer than body, used for balance and defense.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is not visible in this cropped composition; only the head, neck, and shoulder region are shown.

artifact_observations.location: Transition between neck crest and background foliage
artifact_observations.reasoning: Slight softness/blurring at the tips of the dorsal spines where they meet the out-of-focus background. This could be depth-of-field bokeh, but the edges lack the crispness expected of hard keratin spines, suggesting minor generation smoothing.

The geometry of the jaw and cheek area fades into darkness/shadow somewhat unnaturally. The boundary between the subtympanic shield and the rest of the head lacks clear definition, appearing slightly 'melted' or poorly segmented from the shadow.

To verify the structural integrity of the complex dorsal crest and ensure the spines are distinct entities and not fused with the background or each other.

Anatomical correctness of the visible forelimb digits
